newsitem.title: DUBAI: Abu Dhabi to take stake,BICC to cut share in Ducab.
newsitem.headline: Abu Dhabi to take stake,BICC to cut share in Ducab.

text.p: Abu Dhabi emirate plans to take a share in the majority Dubai government-owned Dubai Cable Co (Ducab), while Britain's BICC Plc will reduce its stake, the official UAE news agency WAM said on Wednesday.
It said the move was a first step towards greater industrial cooperation between the neighbours in the seven-member United Arab Emirates federation.

"This initiative is considered a nucleus for the start of participation in joint industrial projects between...Dubai and Abu Dhabi and an integrated step to boost efforts and coordination in setting up industries on state level," WAM said.
It said the restructuring was ahead of a major expansion plan to boost Ducab production and tap more markets worldwide.
Under the plan, 15-year-old Ducab -- a 60-40 joint venture between the Dubai government and BICC -- will become the United Arab Emirates Company for Cables, WAM said.
Through its General Industry Corp, the Abu Dhabi government will hold 35 percent of the firm's equity. Dubai will have 35 percent and BICC will reduce its stake to 30 percent from 40.
Ducab officials would not comment on the report.
The plan, approved by the rulers of Dubai and the oil-rich UAE capital Abu Dhabi was signed by the heads of General Industry Corp and Dubai's Economic Department, it added.
WAM gave no time frame for the changes.
It said the move would help Ducab expand its production base and marketing outlets to become one of the largest cable and wire manufacturers in the Middle East.
The company would seek technology from Europe and the United States and enter into joint ventures with new partners to expand marketing outlets, WAM added.
Ducab sells medium and high-voltage power cables to 80 countries worldwide. Between 1990 and 1995 its sales rose 65 percent and exports went up 15 times, WAM added.
It said 1995 was a record year -- with sales reaching $78 million, 29 percent up on 1994 and exports rising 30 percent.
